{"parentUuid":"2dd1e77f-e038-4d9e-9a97-0af9cd732196","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_btwmvivgoeywqks5jjiimy46","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/sim/sim_test.go","content":"package sim\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/register\"\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/vclock\"\n)\n\nfunc loadExample(t *testing.T, name string) *Scenario {\n\tt.Helper()\n\traw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tvar sc Scenario\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &sc); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn &sc\n}\n\n// Run an example and return its result.\nfunc runExample(t *testing.T, name string) *Result {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tres, err := Run(loadExample(t, name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn res\n}\n\nfunc kinds(r *Result) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(r.Trace))\n\tfor i, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tout[i] = e.Kind\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc contains(haystack []string, needle string) bool {\n\tfor _, s := range haystack {\n\t\tif s == needle {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\nfunc countKinds(r *Result) map[string]int {\n\tm := map[string]int{}\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tm[e.Kind]++\n\t}\n\treturn m\n}\n\n// 01: offline writes diverge, stale overwrite is rejected, full-context\n// merge resolves, gossip converges all nodes.\nfunc TestExampleOfflineWrites(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"01-offline-writes.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.WritesRejected != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejections=%d want 1\", r.Stats.WritesRejected)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.WritesAccepted != 3 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"accepted=%d want 3\", r.Stats.WritesAccepted)\n\t}\n\tks := kinds(r)\n\tif !contains(ks, \"write_rejected\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected a write_rejected trace entry\")\n\t}\n\tfor _, rej := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif rej.Kind == \"write_rejected\" {\n\t\t\tif rej.Reason != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"reason=%s want stale_context\", rej.Reason)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif rej.NewVersion == nil || rej.NewVersion.ID != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejected entry should name the endangered version, got %+v\", rej.NewVersion)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// Every node converges to the single resolved descendant n2#2.\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"profile\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n2#2]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 02: guaranteed duplication; replay must be idempotent.\nfunc TestExampleDuplicates(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"02-duplicate-delivery.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.Duplicates != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"duplicates=%d want 2\", r.Stats.Duplicates)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.Deliveries != 4 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"deliveries=%d want 4\", r.Stats.Deliveries)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tif ns.Node != \"n2\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"n2 final=%v want [n1#2]\", idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// Each duplicated delivery pair: the second merge finds the payload\n\t// already present.\n\tdupDeliveries := 0\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind != \"deliver\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\td := e.Merge[\"k\"]\n\t\tif len(d.Added) == 0 && len(d.Duplicate) > 0 {\n\t\t\tdupDeliveries++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif dupDeliveries != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"idempotent duplicate deliveries=%d want 2\", dupDeliveries)\n\t}\n}\n\n// 03: stale_context and unknown_context both rejected; resolution flows.\nfunc TestExampleStaleContext(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"03-stale-context.json\")\n\treasons := map[string]int{}\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind == \"write_rejected\" {\n\t\t\treasons[e.Reason]++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif reasons[\"stale_context\"] != 1 || reasons[\"unknown_context\"] != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection reasons=%v\", reasons)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.WritesAccepted != 3 || r.Stats.WritesRejected != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"stats=%+v\", r.Stats)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"doc\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n2#2]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 04: reorder — new snapshot arrives first, old snapshot second; the old\n// incoming version is pruned and the register stays at the new version.\nfunc TestExampleReorder(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"04-reorder.json\")\n\tvar firstReachedID string\n\tvar secondPruned []string\n\tdeliveries := 0\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind != \"deliver\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tdeliveries++\n\t\td := e.Merge[\"k\"]\n\t\tif deliveries == 1 {\n\t\t\tif len(d.Added) != 1 || d.Added[0] != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first delivery should add n1#2, got %+v\", d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tfirstReachedID = \"n1#2\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tif deliveries == 2 {\n\t\t\tif len(d.PrunedIncoming) != 1 || d.PrunedIncoming[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late old delivery should prune n1#1, got %+v\", d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tsecondPruned = d.PrunedIncoming\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif firstReachedID != \"n1#2\" || len(secondPruned) != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"reorder not observed correctly (deliveries=%d)\", deliveries)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tif ns.Node == \"n2\" {\n\t\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"n2 final=%v want [n1#2]\", idsOf(vs))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 05: total drop during partition keeps nodes diverged; repair converges.\nfunc TestExampleDropThenRepair(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"05-drop-then-repair.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.Drops != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"drops=%d want 2\", r.Stats.Drops)\n\t}\n\t// Mid-run read at t=10 on n2 sees only its own offline branch.\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind == \"read\" && e.At == 10 {\n\t\t\tif len(e.Siblings) != 1 || e.Siblings[0].ID != \"n2#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"partitioned read=%v want [n2#1]\", idsOf(e.Siblings))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"cfg\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 2 {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want two concurrent siblings\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif idsOf(vs)[0] != \"n1#1\" || idsOf(vs)[1] != \"n2#1\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n1#1 n2#1]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// Determinism: the same seeded scenario run twice produces byte-identical\n// JSON output.\nfunc TestDeterministicAcrossRuns(t *testing.T) {\n\tout1, err := runJSONExample(\"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tout2, err := runJSONExample(\"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif string(out1) != string(out2) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"seeded scenario is not deterministic\")\n\t}\n\t// Different seeds should plausibly differ (defensive: run many).\n\tdiffer := false\n\traw, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", \"06-chaos-seeded.json\"))\n\tfor seed := int64(1); seed < 30; seed++ {\n\t\ts := int64Seed(t, raw, seed)\n\t\to1, err := RunJSON(mustJSON(s))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\ts2 := int64Seed(t, raw, seed+1000)\n\t\to2, err := RunJSON(mustJSON(s2))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif string(o1) != string(o2) {\n\t\t\tdiffer = true\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !differ {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"network RNG appears insensitive to seed\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Convergence under chaos: after enough fault-free gossip rounds, every\n// node must hold exactly the global maximal set of all accepted writes,\n// regardless of which copies were dropped, duplicated or reordered.\nfunc TestChaosConvergence(t *testing.T) {\n\tfor _, seed := range []int64{1, 2, 3, 42, 4242, 9999} {\n\t\tt.Run(\"\", func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tsc := loadExample(t, \"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\t\t\tsc.Name = \"chaos\"\n\t\t\tsc.Seed = seed\n\t\t\tres, err := Run(sc)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// Oracle: take every accepted write version and reduce to the\n\t\t\t// global maximal set.\n\t\t\toracle := map[string]register.Version{}\n\t\t\tfor _, e := range res.Trace {\n\t\t\t\tif e.Kind == \"write\" {\n\t\t\t\t\toracle[e.NewVersion.ID] = *e.NewVersion\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\twant := maximal(t, oracle)\n\n\t\t\t// Continue from the final state: rebuild a fresh scenario whose\n\t\t\t// stores we cannot mutate here, so instead verify via a second\n\t\t\t// healing run using gossip snapshots through the public API by\n\t\t\t// appending repair events to a copy scenario is impossible\n\t\t\t// (stores are internal); instead assert convergence by repeated\n\t\t\t// full broadcasts in an extended scenario.\n\t\t\thealed := healScenario(t, sc, res)\n\t\t\tfinal := healed.FinalState\n\t\t\tfor _, ns := range final {\n\t\t\t\tgot := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\t\t\tif !sameIDSet(idsOf(got), want) {\n\t\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"seed %d node %s=%v want oracle %v\", seed, ns.Node, idsOf(got), want)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\n// healScenario reruns the original events then appends many fault-free\n// broadcasts until a final read tick.\nfunc healScenario(t *testing.T, base *Scenario, first *Result) *Result {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tsc := &Scenario{\n\t\tName:    base.Name,\n\t\tNodes:   append([]string{}, base.Nodes...),\n\t\tSeed:    base.Seed,\n\t\tNetwork: &NetworkConfig{MinDelay: 1, MaxDelay: 1},\n\t\tEvents:  append([]EventSpec{}, base.Events...),\n\t}\n\tat := int64(30)\n\tfor round := 0; round < 6; round++ {\n\t\tfor _, n := range sc.Nodes {\n\t\t\tat++\n\t\t\tsc.Events = append(sc.Events, EventSpec{\n\t\t\t\tAt: at, Type: \"broadcast\", NodeName: n,\n\t\t\t\tDropProb: ptr(0.0), DuplicateProb: ptr(0.0), Delay: ptr(1),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t\tat += 3\n\t}\n\tres, err := Run(sc)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn res\n}\n\nfunc maximal(t *testing.T, vs map[string]register.Version) []string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar all []register.Version\n\tfor _, v := range vs {\n\t\tall = append(all, v)\n\t}\n\tvar out []string\n\tfor i, v := range all {\n\t\tdom := false\n\t\tfor j, w := range all {\n\t\t\tif i == j {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tc := vclock.Compare(v.Clock, w.Clock)\n\t\t\tif c == vclock.Before || (c == vclock.EqualRel && v.ID > w.ID) {\n\t\t\t\tdom = true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !dom {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, v.ID)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn sorted(out)\n}\n\nfunc sameIDSet(got, want []string) bool {\n\tif len(got) != len(want) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tm := map[string]bool{}\n\tfor _, g := range got {\n\t\tm[g] = true\n\t}\n\tfor _, w := range want {\n\t\tif !m[w] {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Validation failures are hard errors, not silent rejections.\nfunc TestValidationErrors(t *testing.T) {\n\tbad := []string{\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[],\"events\":[]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\",\"a\"],\"events\":[]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"events\":[{\"at\":1,\"type\":\"write\",\"node\":\"a\"}]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"events\":[{\"at\":1,\"type\":\"frob\",\"node\":\"a\"}]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"network\":{\"drop_prob\":1.5},\"events\":[]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"events\":[{\"at\":1,\"type\":\"send\",\"node\":\"a\",\"to\":\"b\"}]}`,\n\t}\n\tfor _, b := range bad {\n\t\tvar sc Scenario\n\t\tif err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(b), &sc); err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, err := Run(&sc); err == nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected validation error for %s\", b)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestRunJSONRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {\n\traw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", \"01-offline-writes.json\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tout, err := RunJSON(raw)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif !json.Valid(out) || !strings.Contains(string(out), \"write_rejected\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"output JSON missing expected trace\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// ---- helpers ----\n\nfunc runJSONExample(name string) ([]byte, error) {\n\traw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn RunJSON(raw)\n}\n\nfunc int64Seed(t *testing.T, raw []byte, seed int64) *Scenario {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar sc Scenario\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &sc); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tsc.Seed = seed\n\treturn &sc\n}\n\nfunc mustJSON(sc *Scenario) []byte {\n\tb, _ := json.Marshal(sc)\n\treturn b\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n\nfunc idsOf(vs []register.Version) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(vs))\n\tfor i, v := range vs {\n\t\tout[i] = v.ID\n\t}\n\treturn sorted(out)\n}\n\nfunc sorted(s []string) []string {\n\tfor i := 1; err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn &sc\n}\n\n// Run an example and return its result.\nfunc runExample(t *testing.T, name string) *Result {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tres, err := Run(loadExample(t, name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn res\n}\n\nfunc kinds(r *Result) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(r.Trace))\n\tfor i, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tout[i] = e.Kind\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc contains(haystack []string, needle string) bool {\n\tfor _, s := range haystack {\n\t\tif s == needle {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\nfunc countKinds(r *Result) map[string]int {\n\tm := map[string]int{}\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tm[e.Kind]++\n\t}\n\treturn m\n}\n\n// 01: offline writes diverge, stale overwrite is rejected, full-context\n// merge resolves, gossip converges all nodes.\nfunc TestExampleOfflineWrites(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"01-offline-writes.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.WritesRejected != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejections=%d want 1\", r.Stats.WritesRejected)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.WritesAccepted != 3 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"accepted=%d want 3\", r.Stats.WritesAccepted)\n\t}\n\tks := kinds(r)\n\tif !contains(ks, \"write_rejected\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected a write_rejected trace entry\")\n\t}\n\tfor _, rej := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif rej.Kind == \"write_rejected\" {\n\t\t\tif rej.Reason != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"reason=%s want stale_context\", rej.Reason)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif rej.NewVersion == nil || rej.NewVersion.ID != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejected entry should name the endangered version, got %+v\", rej.NewVersion)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// Every node converges to the single resolved descendant n2#2.\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"profile\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n2#2]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 02: guaranteed duplication; replay must be idempotent.\nfunc TestExampleDuplicates(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"02-duplicate-delivery.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.Duplicates != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"duplicates=%d want 2\", r.Stats.Duplicates)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.Deliveries != 4 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"deliveries=%d want 4\", r.Stats.Deliveries)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tif ns.Node != \"n2\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"n2 final=%v want [n1#2]\", idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// Each duplicated delivery pair: the second merge finds the payload\n\t// already present.\n\tdupDeliveries := 0\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind != \"deliver\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\td := e.Merge[\"k\"]\n\t\tif len(d.Added) == 0 && len(d.Duplicate) > 0 {\n\t\t\tdupDeliveries++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif dupDeliveries != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"idempotent duplicate deliveries=%d want 2\", dupDeliveries)\n\t}\n}\n\n// 03: stale_context and unknown_context both rejected; resolution flows.\nfunc TestExampleStaleContext(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"03-stale-context.json\")\n\treasons := map[string]int{}\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind == \"write_rejected\" {\n\t\t\treasons[e.Reason]++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif reasons[\"stale_context\"] != 1 || reasons[\"unknown_context\"] != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection reasons=%v\", reasons)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.WritesAccepted != 3 || r.Stats.WritesRejected != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"stats=%+v\", r.Stats)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"doc\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n2#2]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 04: reorder — new snapshot arrives first, old snapshot second; the old\n// incoming version is pruned and the register stays at the new version.\nfunc TestExampleReorder(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"04-reorder.json\")\n\tvar firstReachedID string\n\tvar secondPruned []string\n\tdeliveries := 0\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind != \"deliver\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tdeliveries++\n\t\td := e.Merge[\"k\"]\n\t\tif deliveries == 1 {\n\t\t\tif len(d.Added) != 1 || d.Added[0] != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first delivery should add n1#2, got %+v\", d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tfirstReachedID = \"n1#2\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tif deliveries == 2 {\n\t\t\tif len(d.PrunedIncoming) != 1 || d.PrunedIncoming[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late old delivery should prune n1#1, got %+v\", d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tsecondPruned = d.PrunedIncoming\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif firstReachedID != \"n1#2\" || len(secondPruned) != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"reorder not observed correctly (deliveries=%d)\", deliveries)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tif ns.Node == \"n2\" {\n\t\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"n2 final=%v want [n1#2]\", idsOf(vs))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 05: total drop during partition keeps nodes diverged; repair converges.\nfunc TestExampleDropThenRepair(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"05-drop-then-repair.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.Drops != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"drops=%d want 2\", r.Stats.Drops)\n\t}\n\t// Mid-run read at t=10 on n2 sees only its own offline branch.\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind == \"read\" && e.At == 10 {\n\t\t\tif len(e.Siblings) != 1 || e.Siblings[0].ID != \"n2#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"partitioned read=%v want [n2#1]\", idsOf(e.Siblings))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"cfg\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 2 {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want two concurrent siblings\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif idsOf(vs)[0] != \"n1#1\" || idsOf(vs)[1] != \"n2#1\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n1#1 n2#1]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// Determinism: the same seeded scenario run twice produces byte-identical\n// JSON output.\nfunc TestDeterministicAcrossRuns(t *testing.T) {\n\tout1, err := runJSONExample(\"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tout2, err := runJSONExample(\"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif string(out1) != string(out2) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"seeded scenario is not deterministic\")\n\t}\n\t// Different seeds should plausibly differ (defensive: run many).\n\tdiffer := false\n\traw, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", \"06-chaos-seeded.json\"))\n\tfor seed := int64(1); seed < 30; seed++ {\n\t\ts := int64Seed(t, raw, seed)\n\t\to1, err := RunJSON(mustJSON(s))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\ts2 := int64Seed(t, raw, seed+1000)\n\t\to2, err := RunJSON(mustJSON(s2))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif string(o1) != string(o2) {\n\t\t\tdiffer = true\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !differ {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"network RNG appears insensitive to seed\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Convergence under chaos: after enough fault-free gossip rounds, every\n// node must hold exactly the global maximal set of all accepted writes,\n// regardless of which copies were dropped, duplicated or reordered.\nfunc TestChaosConvergence(t *testing.T) {\n\tfor _, seed := range []int64{1, 2, 3, 42, 4242, 9999} {\n\t\tt.Run(\"\", func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tsc := loadExample(t, \"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\t\t\tsc.Name = \"chaos\"\n\t\t\tsc.Seed = seed\n\t\t\tres, err := Run(sc)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// Oracle: take every accepted write version and reduce to the\n\t\t\t// global maximal set.\n\t\t\toracle := map[string]register.Version{}\n\t\t\tfor _, e := range res.Trace {\n\t\t\t\tif e.Kind == \"write\" {\n\t\t\t\t\toracle[e.NewVersion.ID] = *e.NewVersion\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\twant := maximal(t, oracle)\n\n\t\t\t// Continue from the final state: rebuild a fresh scenario whose\n\t\t\t// stores we cannot mutate here, so instead verify via a second\n\t\t\t// healing run using gossip snapshots through the public API by\n\t\t\t// appending repair events to a copy scenario is impossible\n\t\t\t// (stores are internal); instead assert convergence by repeated\n\t\t\t// full broadcasts in an extended scenario.\n\t\t\thealed := healScenario(t, sc, res)\n\t\t\tfinal := healed.FinalState\n\t\t\tfor _, ns := range final {\n\t\t\t\tgot := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\t\t\tif !sameIDSet(idsOf(got), want) {\n\t\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"seed %d node %s=%v want oracle %v\", seed, ns.Node, idsOf(got), want)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\n// healScenario reruns the original events then appends many fault-free\n// broadcasts until a final read tick.\nfunc healScenario(t *testing.T, base *Scenario, first *Result) *Result {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tsc := &Scenario{\n\t\tName:    base.Name,\n\t\tNodes:   append([]string{}, base.Nodes...),\n\t\tSeed:    base.Seed,\n\t\tNetwork: &NetworkConfig{MinDelay: 1, MaxDelay: 1},\n\t\tEvents:  append([]EventSpec{}, base.Events...),\n\t}\n\tat := int64(30)\n\tfor round := 0; err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tsc.Seed = seed\n\treturn &sc\n}\n\nfunc mustJSON(sc *Scenario) []byte {\n\tb, _ := json.Marshal(sc)\n\treturn b\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n\nfunc idsOf(vs []register.Version) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(vs))\n\tfor i, v := range vs {\n\t\tout[i] = v.ID\n\t}\n\treturn sorted(out)\n}\n\nfunc sorted(s []string) []string {\n\tfor i := 1; i < len(s); i++ {\n\t\tfor j := i; j > 0 && s[j-1] > s[j]; j-- {\n\t\t\ts[j-1], s[j] = s[j], s[j-1]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n","file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/sim/sim_test.go"}},"apiBlockIndex":1,"type":"assistant","uuid":"7ffffce8-b407-47e0-9269-4bfdf4147895","timestamp":"2026-09-23T04:56:38.605Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"c4de3418-a88f-4832-8733-858ef662dc1b","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b","sessionId":"c4de3418-a88f-4832-8733-858ef662dc1b","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp24-b","slug":"mossy-waddling-steele"}

{"parentUuid":"7ffffce8-b407-47e0-9269-4bfdf4147895","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b6f84a6b-b0a7-4281-bbb6-b9695f2c23bd","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_btwmvivgoeywqks5jjiimy46","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/sim/sim_test.go (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"13d8e7cf-7bc2-44b0-a5f3-b0600a889c2c","timestamp":"2026-09-23T04:56:38.635Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/sim/sim_test.go","content":"package sim\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/register\"\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/vclock\"\n)\n\nfunc loadExample(t *testing.T, name string) *Scenario {\n\tt.Helper()\n\traw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tvar sc Scenario\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &sc); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn &sc\n}\n\n// Run an example and return its result.\nfunc runExample(t *testing.T, name string) *Result {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tres, err := Run(loadExample(t, name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn res\n}\n\nfunc kinds(r *Result) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(r.Trace))\n\tfor i, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tout[i] = e.Kind\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc contains(haystack []string, needle string) bool {\n\tfor _, s := range haystack {\n\t\tif s == needle {\n\t\t\treturn true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false\n}\n\nfunc countKinds(r *Result) map[string]int {\n\tm := map[string]int{}\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tm[e.Kind]++\n\t}\n\treturn m\n}\n\n// 01: offline writes diverge, stale overwrite is rejected, full-context\n// merge resolves, gossip converges all nodes.\nfunc TestExampleOfflineWrites(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"01-offline-writes.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.WritesRejected != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejections=%d want 1\", r.Stats.WritesRejected)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.WritesAccepted != 3 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"accepted=%d want 3\", r.Stats.WritesAccepted)\n\t}\n\tks := kinds(r)\n\tif !contains(ks, \"write_rejected\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected a write_rejected trace entry\")\n\t}\n\tfor _, rej := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif rej.Kind == \"write_rejected\" {\n\t\t\tif rej.Reason != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"reason=%s want stale_context\", rej.Reason)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif rej.NewVersion == nil || rej.NewVersion.ID != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejected entry should name the endangered version, got %+v\", rej.NewVersion)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// Every node converges to the single resolved descendant n2#2.\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"profile\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n2#2]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 02: guaranteed duplication; replay must be idempotent.\nfunc TestExampleDuplicates(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"02-duplicate-delivery.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.Duplicates != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"duplicates=%d want 2\", r.Stats.Duplicates)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.Deliveries != 4 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"deliveries=%d want 4\", r.Stats.Deliveries)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tif ns.Node != \"n2\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"n2 final=%v want [n1#2]\", idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\t// Each duplicated delivery pair: the second merge finds the payload\n\t// already present.\n\tdupDeliveries := 0\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind != \"deliver\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\td := e.Merge[\"k\"]\n\t\tif len(d.Added) == 0 && len(d.Duplicate) > 0 {\n\t\t\tdupDeliveries++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif dupDeliveries != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"idempotent duplicate deliveries=%d want 2\", dupDeliveries)\n\t}\n}\n\n// 03: stale_context and unknown_context both rejected; resolution flows.\nfunc TestExampleStaleContext(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"03-stale-context.json\")\n\treasons := map[string]int{}\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind == \"write_rejected\" {\n\t\t\treasons[e.Reason]++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif reasons[\"stale_context\"] != 1 || reasons[\"unknown_context\"] != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection reasons=%v\", reasons)\n\t}\n\tif r.Stats.WritesAccepted != 3 || r.Stats.WritesRejected != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"stats=%+v\", r.Stats)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"doc\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n2#2]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 04: reorder — new snapshot arrives first, old snapshot second; the old\n// incoming version is pruned and the register stays at the new version.\nfunc TestExampleReorder(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"04-reorder.json\")\n\tvar firstReachedID string\n\tvar secondPruned []string\n\tdeliveries := 0\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind != \"deliver\" {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tdeliveries++\n\t\td := e.Merge[\"k\"]\n\t\tif deliveries == 1 {\n\t\t\tif len(d.Added) != 1 || d.Added[0] != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first delivery should add n1#2, got %+v\", d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tfirstReachedID = \"n1#2\"\n\t\t}\n\t\tif deliveries == 2 {\n\t\t\tif len(d.PrunedIncoming) != 1 || d.PrunedIncoming[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late old delivery should prune n1#1, got %+v\", d)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tsecondPruned = d.PrunedIncoming\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif firstReachedID != \"n1#2\" || len(secondPruned) != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"reorder not observed correctly (deliveries=%d)\", deliveries)\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tif ns.Node == \"n2\" {\n\t\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\t\tif len(vs) != 1 || vs[0].ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"n2 final=%v want [n1#2]\", idsOf(vs))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// 05: total drop during partition keeps nodes diverged; repair converges.\nfunc TestExampleDropThenRepair(t *testing.T) {\n\tr := runExample(t, \"05-drop-then-repair.json\")\n\tif r.Stats.Drops != 2 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"drops=%d want 2\", r.Stats.Drops)\n\t}\n\t// Mid-run read at t=10 on n2 sees only its own offline branch.\n\tfor _, e := range r.Trace {\n\t\tif e.Kind == \"read\" && e.At == 10 {\n\t\t\tif len(e.Siblings) != 1 || e.Siblings[0].ID != \"n2#1\" {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"partitioned read=%v want [n2#1]\", idsOf(e.Siblings))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor _, ns := range r.FinalState {\n\t\tvs := ns.Keys[\"cfg\"]\n\t\tif len(vs) != 2 {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want two concurrent siblings\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif idsOf(vs)[0] != \"n1#1\" || idsOf(vs)[1] != \"n2#1\" {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"node %s final=%v want [n1#1 n2#1]\", ns.Node, idsOf(vs))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// Determinism: the same seeded scenario run twice produces byte-identical\n// JSON output.\nfunc TestDeterministicAcrossRuns(t *testing.T) {\n\tout1, err := runJSONExample(\"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tout2, err := runJSONExample(\"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif string(out1) != string(out2) {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"seeded scenario is not deterministic\")\n\t}\n\t// Different seeds should plausibly differ (defensive: run many).\n\tdiffer := false\n\traw, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", \"06-chaos-seeded.json\"))\n\tfor seed := int64(1); seed < 30; seed++ {\n\t\ts := int64Seed(t, raw, seed)\n\t\to1, err := RunJSON(mustJSON(s))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\ts2 := int64Seed(t, raw, seed+1000)\n\t\to2, err := RunJSON(mustJSON(s2))\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif string(o1) != string(o2) {\n\t\t\tdiffer = true\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !differ {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"network RNG appears insensitive to seed\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Convergence under chaos: after enough fault-free gossip rounds, every\n// node must hold exactly the global maximal set of all accepted writes,\n// regardless of which copies were dropped, duplicated or reordered.\nfunc TestChaosConvergence(t *testing.T) {\n\tfor _, seed := range []int64{1, 2, 3, 42, 4242, 9999} {\n\t\tt.Run(\"\", func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tsc := loadExample(t, \"06-chaos-seeded.json\")\n\t\t\tsc.Name = \"chaos\"\n\t\t\tsc.Seed = seed\n\t\t\tres, err := Run(sc)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\t// Oracle: take every accepted write version and reduce to the\n\t\t\t// global maximal set.\n\t\t\toracle := map[string]register.Version{}\n\t\t\tfor _, e := range res.Trace {\n\t\t\t\tif e.Kind == \"write\" {\n\t\t\t\t\toracle[e.NewVersion.ID] = *e.NewVersion\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\twant := maximal(t, oracle)\n\n\t\t\t// Continue from the final state: rebuild a fresh scenario whose\n\t\t\t// stores we cannot mutate here, so instead verify via a second\n\t\t\t// healing run using gossip snapshots through the public API by\n\t\t\t// appending repair events to a copy scenario is impossible\n\t\t\t// (stores are internal); instead assert convergence by repeated\n\t\t\t// full broadcasts in an extended scenario.\n\t\t\thealed := healScenario(t, sc, res)\n\t\t\tfinal := healed.FinalState\n\t\t\tfor _, ns := range final {\n\t\t\t\tgot := ns.Keys[\"k\"]\n\t\t\t\tif !sameIDSet(idsOf(got), want) {\n\t\t\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"seed %d node %s=%v want oracle %v\", seed, ns.Node, idsOf(got), want)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\n// healScenario reruns the original events then appends many fault-free\n// broadcasts until a final read tick.\nfunc healScenario(t *testing.T, base *Scenario, first *Result) *Result {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tsc := &Scenario{\n\t\tName:    base.Name,\n\t\tNodes:   append([]string{}, base.Nodes...),\n\t\tSeed:    base.Seed,\n\t\tNetwork: &NetworkConfig{MinDelay: 1, MaxDelay: 1},\n\t\tEvents:  append([]EventSpec{}, base.Events...),\n\t}\n\tat := int64(30)\n\tfor round := 0; round < 6; round++ {\n\t\tfor _, n := range sc.Nodes {\n\t\t\tat++\n\t\t\tsc.Events = append(sc.Events, EventSpec{\n\t\t\t\tAt: at, Type: \"broadcast\", NodeName: n,\n\t\t\t\tDropProb: ptr(0.0), DuplicateProb: ptr(0.0), Delay: ptr(1),\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t\tat += 3\n\t}\n\tres, err := Run(sc)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\treturn res\n}\n\nfunc maximal(t *testing.T, vs map[string]register.Version) []string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar all []register.Version\n\tfor _, v := range vs {\n\t\tall = append(all, v)\n\t}\n\tvar out []string\n\tfor i, v := range all {\n\t\tdom := false\n\t\tfor j, w := range all {\n\t\t\tif i == j {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tc := vclock.Compare(v.Clock, w.Clock)\n\t\t\tif c == vclock.Before || (c == vclock.EqualRel && v.ID > w.ID) {\n\t\t\t\tdom = true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !dom {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, v.ID)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn sorted(out)\n}\n\nfunc sameIDSet(got, want []string) bool {\n\tif len(got) != len(want) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tm := map[string]bool{}\n\tfor _, g := range got {\n\t\tm[g] = true\n\t}\n\tfor _, w := range want {\n\t\tif !m[w] {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// Validation failures are hard errors, not silent rejections.\nfunc TestValidationErrors(t *testing.T) {\n\tbad := []string{\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[],\"events\":[]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\",\"a\"],\"events\":[]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"events\":[{\"at\":1,\"type\":\"write\",\"node\":\"a\"}]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"events\":[{\"at\":1,\"type\":\"frob\",\"node\":\"a\"}]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"network\":{\"drop_prob\":1.5},\"events\":[]}`,\n\t\t`{\"name\":\"x\",\"nodes\":[\"a\"],\"events\":[{\"at\":1,\"type\":\"send\",\"node\":\"a\",\"to\":\"b\"}]}`,\n\t}\n\tfor _, b := range bad {\n\t\tvar sc Scenario\n\t\tif err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(b), &sc); err != nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif _, err := Run(&sc); err == nil {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected validation error for %s\", b)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestRunJSONRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {\n\traw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", \"01-offline-writes.json\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tout, err := RunJSON(raw)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif !json.Valid(out) || !strings.Contains(string(out), \"write_rejected\") {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"output JSON missing expected trace\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// ---- helpers ----\n\nfunc runJSONExample(name string) ([]byte, error) {\n\traw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(\"..\", \"..\", \"examples\", name))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn RunJSON(raw)\n}\n\nfunc int64Seed(t *testing.T, raw []byte, seed int64) *Scenario {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar sc Scenario\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &sc); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tsc.Seed = seed\n\treturn &sc\n}\n\nfunc mustJSON(sc *Scenario) []byte {\n\tb, _ := json.Marshal(sc)\n\treturn b\n}\n\nfunc ptr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }\n\nfunc idsOf(vs []register.Version) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(vs))\n\tfor i, v := range vs {\n\t\tout[i] = v.ID\n\t}\n\treturn sorted(out)\n}\n\nfunc sorted(s []string) []string {\n\tfor i := 1; i < len(s); i++ {\n\t\tfor j := i; j > 0 && s[j-1] > s[j]; j-- {\n\t\t\ts[j-1], s[j] = s[j], s[j-1]\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"7ffffce8-b407-47e0-9269-4bfdf4147895","session_id":"c4de3418-a88f-4832-8733-858ef662dc1b","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b","sessionId":"c4de3418-a88f-4832-8733-858ef662dc1b","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp24-b","slug":"mossy-waddling-steele"}

{"parentUuid":"1374067a-bfe0-4d1d-9b8c-25e9aece4745","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"signature":"","thinking":"Several issues:1. Three code issues have been identified and will be fixed in sequence: First, a syntax error in the merged input check will be corrected by adding parentheses around the composite literal in the index expression; second, the return value of the ptr function will be adjusted to use int64 as the parameter type; third, the abnormal behavior of the offline write test will be traced and confirmed to be a pre-existing defect that needs to be addressed.\n\nThe root cause of the TestOfflineWritesThenMerge test's abnormal behavior has been identified: the corresponding write was not marked as stale and was incorrectly accepted.\n\nFurther analysis reveals that this incorrectly accepted write generates a sibling entry instead of overwriting the existing one, with no data loss caused by the conflict.\n\nFurther analysis of the VC consistency rule shows that a stale write only overwrites an existing entry when there are unseen versions it can dominate. For versions it cannot dominate, only new concurrent branches are created, with no write safety risks.\n\nIt has been confirmed that the scenario where a stale write overwrites an existing entry only occurs when the version clock of the write author is lower than the current node's clock, which triggers an ID collision. My previous test expectation for cross-node blind writes was incorrect, and such operations will cause concurrent forks.\n\nRejection design for the old context coverage scenario needs reconsideration. Pure VV semantics naturally preserve concurrent versions as siblings without silent data loss, so no rejection mechanism is required for this case, and the eventual consistency handling is correct.\n\nThe stale context rejection only triggers for self-author clock collision cases. I've confirmed pure VV semantics only require rejection for genuine silent loss risks, with no extra rejection mechanism needed for normal old context coverage scenarios, and all concurrent version data loss prevention guarantees are fully covered.\n\nAfter in-depth verification, I've confirmed that the scenario where a pure-VV context write silently dominates an unseen concurrent version only occurs when the write author's local self-version is not included in the client's context, and the corresponding rejection rule is logically valid. My previous stale check condition is indeed too narrow in scope.\n\nMy earlier example for the stale context overwrite scenario is invalid, as it only creates a concurrent sibling without silent data loss. I've clarified two verification scenarios to prove no silent loss occurs with stale context writes, and will build the same-node demo next.\n\nThe same-node stale write is explicitly rejected, while cross-node stale writes only trigger conflicts and retain concurrent versions, with no silent data loss. a merge write with the\n// full context replaces both with one descendant.\nfunc TestOfflineWritesThenMerge(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"A\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Cross-node stale context (client only saw n2#1) does NOT silently\n\t// overwrite n1#1: the new clock {n2:2} is concurrent with {n1:1},\n\t// so the unseen version survives as an extra sibling branch.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"fork\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"concurrent fork should be accepted, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#3\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolution propagates: n1's n1#1 gets pruned on merge.\n\tr := n1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.Pruned) != 1 || r.Pruned[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"merge pruned=%v want [n1#1]\", r.Pruned)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n}\n\n// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. a merge write with the\n// full context replaces both with one descendant.\nfunc TestOfflineWritesThenMerge(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"A\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Stale context (only own sibling) must be rejected: n1#1 would be lost.\n\t_, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"stale\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif rejectReason(t, err) != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want stale_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\") // unchanged\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 2}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n}\n\n// A context naming an unknown version is rejected and changes nothing.\nfunc TestUnknownContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\tif _, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\t_, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"ghost#7\"})\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &rej) || rej.Reason != \"unknown_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want unknown_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\")\n}\n\n// Replaying the same snapshot is idempotent; merge order does not change\n// the final maximal set; dominated incoming versions are discarded.\nfunc TestMergeIdempotentAndOrderIndependent(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`1`), nil)\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`2`), nil)\n\n\ts1 := n1.Snapshot()\n\tr1 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r1.Added) != 1 || len(r1.Duplicate) != 0 || len(r1.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first merge=%+v\", r1)\n\t}\n\tr2 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r2.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r2.Added) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"replay merge=%+v\", r2)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// n1 merges n2's branch in, then writes with full context.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())\n\trep, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`1+2`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\t_ = rep\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\")\n\n\tr3 := n1.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"] // stale snapshot replay\n\tif len(r3.PrunedIncoming) != 1 || len(r3.Added) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"stale merge=%+v\", r3)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\")\n\n\t// Symmetric: n2 receiving n1#2 converges.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\")\n}\n\n// Cross-node stale write (the textbook case): writer on n3 saw only an\n// older ancestor of the version it would dominate.\nfunc TestCrossNodeStaleContext(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n3 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n3\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`1`), nil)\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot()) // n3 has n1#1\n\n\t// n1 evolves the value with n1#1 as context.\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`2`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot()) // n3 now has n1#2\n\n\t// n1 writes again offline -> n1#3 descends from n1#2; n3 does not know it.\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`3`), []string{\"n1#2\"})\n\n\t// n3 merges with the stale context [n1#1] (which it did observe, so\n\t// the IDs resolve), producing n3#1 dominating n1#1 and n3's joined\n\t// view — but n1#3 is concurrent, not dominated, so it survives.\n\trep, err := n3.Write(\"k\", raw(`from n3`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"cross-node branch should be allowed, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n3.Read(\"k\"), rep.NewVersion.ID) // n1#2 pruned as transitive ancestor\n\n\t// After n1#3 gossips in, both branches coexist as siblings.\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n3.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#3\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n}\n\n// Snapshot copies are independent: mutating one store cannot affect a\n// snapshot taken earlier or another replica merged from it.\nfunc TestSnapshotIsolation(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil)\n\tsnap := n1.Snapshot()\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(snap)\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\")\n\tif got := snap.Versions[\"k\"][0].Value; err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Cross-node stale context (client only saw n2#1) does NOT silently\n\t// overwrite n1#1: the new clock {n2:2} is concurrent with {n1:1},\n\t// so the unseen version survives as an extra sibling branch.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"fork\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"concurrent fork should be accepted, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#3\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolution propagates: n1's n1#1 gets pruned on merge.\n\tr := n1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.Pruned) != 1 || r.Pruned[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"merge pruned=%v want [n1#1]\", r.Pruned)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n}\n\n// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. n1#2 (unseen, same author) would be silently\n\t// dominated, so the store refuses.\n\t_, err = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"c\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif rejectReason(t, err) != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want stale_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\terrors.As(err, &rej)\n\tif rej.StaleUnseen == nil || rej.StaleUnseen.ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection should name n1#2 as endangered, got %+v\", rej.StaleUnseen)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\") // store unchanged\n}","originalFile":"package register\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/vclock\"\n)\n\nfunc ids(vs []Version) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(vs))\n\tfor i, v := range vs {\n\t\tout[i] = v.ID\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc expectIDs(t *testing.T, got []Version, want ...string) {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tif len(got) != len(want) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"versions=%v want %v\", ids(got), want)\n\t}\n\tfor i, w := range want {\n\t\tif got[i].ID != w {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"versions=%v want %v\", ids(got), want)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc raw(s string) json.RawMessage { return json.RawMessage(s) }\n\nfunc rejectReason(t *testing.T, err error) string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &rej) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected RejectError, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn rej.Reason\n}\n\n// Concurrent offline writes are kept as siblings; a merge write with the\n// full context replaces both with one descendant.\nfunc TestOfflineWritesThenMerge(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"A\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Cross-node stale context (client only saw n2#1) does NOT silently\n\t// overwrite n1#1: the new clock {n2:2} is concurrent with {n1:1},\n\t// so the unseen version survives as an extra sibling branch.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"fork\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"concurrent fork should be accepted, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#3\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolution propagates: n1's n1#1 gets pruned on merge.\n\tr := n1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.Pruned) != 1 || r.Pruned[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"merge pruned=%v want [n1#1]\", r.Pruned)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n}\n\n// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. That is\n// rejected instead.\nfunc TestSameAuthorStaleContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\t_, _ = n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil) // n1#1\n\t_, _ = n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2\n\n\t// New node n3 learned n1#2 directly (e.g. the client read it there);\n\t// n1 itself never \"lost\" n1#2 — simulate the dangerous window: n1#2\n\t// exists locally but the writer pretends it never saw it.\n\t_, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"c\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif rejectReason(t, err) != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want stale_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\terrors.As(err, &rej)\n\tif rej.StaleUnseen == nil || rej.StaleUnseen.ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection should name n1#2 as endangered, got %+v\", rej.StaleUnseen)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\") // store unchanged\n}\n\n// A context naming an unknown version is rejected and changes nothing.\nfunc TestUnknownContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\tif _, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\t_, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"ghost#7\"})\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &rej) || rej.Reason != \"unknown_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want unknown_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\")\n}\n\n// Invalid JSON payloads are rejected.\nfunc TestInvalidValueRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\tif _, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`not json`), nil); err == nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected error for invalid JSON\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Replaying the same snapshot is idempotent; dominated versions arriving\n// late (reordering) are pruned on arrival rather than resurrected.\nfunc TestMergeIdempotentAndReorder(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil)\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), nil)\n\n\ts1 := n1.Snapshot()\n\tr1 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r1.Added) != 1 || len(r1.Duplicate) != 0 || len(r1.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first merge=%+v\", r1)\n\t}\n\tr2 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r2.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r2.Added) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"replay merge=%+v\", r2)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// n2 resolves; then the OLD snapshot {n1#1} arrives late. n1#1 is\n\t// already known to n2 and now dominated: it's a no-op duplicate.\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1+2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"}); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\tr3 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r3.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r3.Added) != 0 || len(r3.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late stale replay=%+v\", r3)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\n\t// A genuinely OLD node receiving a descendant snapshot prunes the\n\t// ancestor locally.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n}\n\n// Cross-node stale write forks; the offline branch survives gossip and\n// stays concurrent — nothing is silently lost.\nfunc TestCrossNodeStaleWriteForks(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n3 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n3\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil) // n1#1\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())        // n3: [n1#1]\n\n\t// n1 evolves twice locally; n3 does not see either.\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"3\"`), []string{\"n1#2\"}) // n1#3\n\n\t// n3 writes from the stale context [n1#1]. The merge\n// treats them as transitive coverage.\nfunc TestTransitiveAncestorPrune(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil)              // n1#1\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"off\"`), nil)             // n2#1\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())                     // n2: [n1#1, n2#1]\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2 (n1 hasn't seen n2#1)\n\n\t// n2 merges n1#2 (siblings n1#2/n2#1), then writes from a context\n\t// naming only n1#1 + n2#1: n1#2 is dominated by the join and is\n\t// pruned as transitive coverage rather than rejecting the write.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\", \"n2#1\")\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"join\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif len(rep.Transitive) != 1 || rep.Transitive[0] != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"transitive prune=%v want [n1#2]\", rep.Transitive)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), rep.NewVersion.ID)\n}","originalFile":"package register\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/vclock\"\n)\n\nfunc ids(vs []Version) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(vs))\n\tfor i, v := range vs {\n\t\tout[i] = v.ID\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc expectIDs(t *testing.T, got []Version, want ...string) {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tif len(got) != len(want) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"versions=%v want %v\", ids(got), want)\n\t}\n\tfor i, w := range want {\n\t\tif got[i].ID != w {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"versions=%v want %v\", ids(got), want)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc raw(s string) json.RawMessage { return json.RawMessage(s) }\n\nfunc rejectReason(t *testing.T, err error) string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &rej) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected RejectError, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn rej.Reason\n}\n\n// Concurrent offline writes are kept as siblings; a merge write with the\n// full context replaces both with one descendant.\nfunc TestOfflineWritesThenMerge(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"A\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Cross-node stale context (client only saw n2#1) does NOT silently\n\t// overwrite n1#1: the new clock {n2:2} is concurrent with {n1:1},\n\t// so the unseen version survives as an extra sibling branch.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"fork\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"concurrent fork should be accepted, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#3\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolution propagates: n1's n1#1 gets pruned on merge.\n\tr := n1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.Pruned) != 1 || r.Pruned[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"merge pruned=%v want [n1#1]\", r.Pruned)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n}\n\n// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. That is\n// rejected instead. The realistic window is a node that re-joined after\n// another replica advanced its self-counter through a merge write.\nfunc TestSameAuthorStaleContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil) // n1#1\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())        // n2: [n1#1]\n\n\t// n2 performs the merge write on n1's behalf (DVV-style), advancing\n\t// n1's self counter: n1#2 descends from n1#1.\n\t_, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\t// That resolution has not yet reached n1. n1 writes again from the\n\t// stale context [n1#1]; n1#2 (unseen, same author) would be silently\n\t// dominated, so the store refuses.\n\t_, err = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"c\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif rejectReason(t, err) != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want stale_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\terrors.As(err, &rej)\n\tif rej.StaleUnseen == nil || rej.StaleUnseen.ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection should name n1#2 as endangered, got %+v\", rej.StaleUnseen)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\") // store unchanged\n}\n\n// A context naming an unknown version is rejected and changes nothing.\nfunc TestUnknownContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\tif _, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil); err == nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected error for invalid JSON\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Replaying the same snapshot is idempotent; dominated versions arriving\n// late (reordering) are pruned on arrival rather than resurrected.\nfunc TestMergeIdempotentAndReorder(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil)\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), nil)\n\n\ts1 := n1.Snapshot()\n\tr1 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r1.Added) != 1 || len(r1.Duplicate) != 0 || len(r1.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first merge=%+v\", r1)\n\t}\n\tr2 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r2.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r2.Added) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"replay merge=%+v\", r2)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// n2 resolves; then the OLD snapshot {n1#1} arrives late. n1#1 is\n\t// already known to n2 and now dominated: it's a no-op duplicate.\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1+2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"}); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\tr3 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r3.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r3.Added) != 0 || len(r3.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late stale replay=%+v\", r3)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\n\t// A genuinely OLD node receiving a descendant snapshot prunes the\n\t// ancestor locally.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n}\n\n// Cross-node stale write forks; the offline branch survives gossip and\n// stays concurrent — nothing is silently lost.\nfunc TestCrossNodeStaleWriteForks(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n3 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n3\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil) // n1#1\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())        // n3: [n1#1]\n\n\t// n1 evolves twice locally; n3 does not see either.\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"3\"`), []string{\"n1#2\"}) // n1#3\n\n\t// n3 writes from the stale context [n1#1]. New clock {n1:1,n3:1} is\n\t// concurrent with n1#3 {n1:3} -> fork, n1#1 pruned transitively.\n\trep, err := n3.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"from n3\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"cross-node fork should be allowed, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n3.Read(\"k\"), rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Gossip from n1: n1#3 joins as a sibling; the stale n1#1 is gone.\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n3.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#3\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n}\n\n// Observed-but-stale ancestors (versions dominated by the joined context)\n// may legitimately be pruned even when not explicitly named.\nfunc TestTransitiveAncestorPrune(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil) // n1#1\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())        // n2: [n1#1]\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())        // n2: [n1#2]\n\n\t// n2 has seen n1#2 via gossip, but the client's context only names\n\t// n1#1 (which it read earlier) plus n2's own independent branch.\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"off\"`), nil) // n2#1\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"join\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif len(rep.Transitive) != 1 || rep.Transitive[0] != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"transitive prune=%v want [n1#2]\", rep.Transitive)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), rep.NewVersion.ID)\n}\n\n// Snapshot copies are independent of later store mutation.\nfunc TestSnapshotIsolation(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil)\n\tsnap := n1.Snapshot()\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(snap)\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\")\n\tif got := snap.Versions[\"k\"][0].Value; the point is the join\n\t// succeeds and no stale rejection fires for dominated ancestors.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"join\"`), []string{\"n2#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Conversely: an ancestor arriving late via gossip is pruned without\n\t// blocking a write whose context covers its descendants.\n\tn3 := NewStore(\"n3\")\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot()) // sees only descendant n2#3\n\told := Snapshot{Versions: map[string][]Version{\n\t\t\"k\": {{ID: \"n1#1\", Value: raw(`\"1\"`), Clock: vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1}, Author: \"n1\"}},\n\t}}\n\tr := n3.MergeSnapshot(old)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.PrunedIncoming) != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late ancestor merge=%+v\", r)\n\t}\n}"},"name":"Edit","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_61f174f2e7f1e5a2772e2cea","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":2848,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":75576,"output_tokens":1380,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_kgtz1wke0bl7rrvw186kmpa6":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/register/register_test.go","new_string":"// Observed-but-stale ancestors (versions dominated by the joined context)\n// may legitimately be pruned even when not explicitly named. Meanwhile n2\n\t// branched independently (n2#2 {n2:2}) and both are local siblings.\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"branch\"`), nil) // n2#2 {n2:2}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#1\", \"n2#2\")\n\n\t// Client merges n2#1 (whose clock already covers n1#1) with n2#2,\n\t// redundantly also naming the ancestor n1#1. n1#1 no longer exists in\n\t// the store (pruned when n2#1 was written); the point is the join\n\t// succeeds and no stale rejection fires for dominated ancestors.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"join\"`), []string{\"n2#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Conversely: an ancestor arriving late via gossip is pruned without\n\t// blocking a write whose context covers its descendants.\n\tn3 := NewStore(\"n3\")\n\tn3.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot()) // sees only descendant n2#3\n\told := Snapshot{Versions: map[string][]Version{\n\t\t\"k\": {{ID: \"n1#1\", Value: raw(`\"1\"`), Clock: vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1}, Author: \"n1\"}},\n\t}}\n\tr := n3.MergeSnapshot(old)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.PrunedIncoming) != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late ancestor merge=%+v\", r)\n\t}\n}","originalFile":"package register\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/json\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"testing\"\n\n\t\"vcconflict/internal/vclock\"\n)\n\nfunc ids(vs []Version) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, len(vs))\n\tfor i, v := range vs {\n\t\tout[i] = v.ID\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\nfunc expectIDs(t *testing.T, got []Version, want ...string) {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tif len(got) != len(want) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"versions=%v want %v\", ids(got), want)\n\t}\n\tfor i, w := range want {\n\t\tif got[i].ID != w {\n\t\t\tt.Fatalf(\"versions=%v want %v\", ids(got), want)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc raw(s string) json.RawMessage { return json.RawMessage(s) }\n\nfunc rejectReason(t *testing.T, err error) string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &rej) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected RejectError, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn rej.Reason\n}\n\n// Concurrent offline writes are kept as siblings; a merge write with the\n// full context replaces both with one descendant.\nfunc TestOfflineWritesThenMerge(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"A\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Cross-node stale context (client only saw n2#1) does NOT silently\n\t// overwrite n1#1: the new clock {n2:2} is concurrent with {n1:1},\n\t// so the unseen version survives as an extra sibling branch.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"fork\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"concurrent fork should be accepted, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#3\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolution propagates: n1's n1#1 gets pruned on merge.\n\tr := n1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.Pruned) != 1 || r.Pruned[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"merge pruned=%v want [n1#1]\", r.Pruned)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n}\n\n// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. That is\n// rejected instead. The realistic window is a node that re-joined after\n// another replica advanced its self-counter through a merge write.\nfunc TestSameAuthorStaleContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil) // n1#1\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())        // n2: [n1#1]\n\n\t// n2 performs the merge write on n1's behalf (DVV-style), advancing\n\t// n1's self counter: n1#2 descends from n1#1.\n\t_, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\t// That resolution has not yet reached n1. n1 writes again from the\n\t// stale context [n1#1]; n1#2 (unseen, same author) would be silently\n\t// dominated, so the store refuses.\n\t_, err = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"c\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif rejectReason(t, err) != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want stale_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\terrors.As(err, &rej)\n\tif rej.StaleUnseen == nil || rej.StaleUnseen.ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection should name n1#2 as endangered, got %+v\", rej.StaleUnseen)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\") // store unchanged\n}\n\n// A context naming an unknown version is rejected and changes nothing.\nfunc TestUnknownContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\tif _, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\t_, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"b\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"ghost#7\"})\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &rej) || rej.Reason != \"unknown_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want unknown_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\")\n}\n\n// Invalid JSON payloads are rejected.\nfunc TestInvalidValueRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\tif _, err := n.Write(\"k\", raw(`not json`), nil); err == nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected error for invalid JSON\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// Replaying the same snapshot is idempotent; dominated versions arriving\n// late (reordering) are pruned on arrival rather than resurrected.\nfunc TestMergeIdempotentAndReorder(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1\"`), nil)\n\t_, _ = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), nil)\n\n\ts1 := n1.Snapshot()\n\tr1 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r1.Added) != 1 || len(r1.Duplicate) != 0 || len(r1.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"first merge=%+v\", r1)\n\t}\n\tr2 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r2.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r2.Added) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"replay merge=%+v\", r2)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// n2 resolves; {"parentUuid":"e36bd8b3-9f80-444b-96b8-10c72ee07a9a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_7w7oi3rwond2gfixz4jj6ayt","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/register/register_test.go","old_string":"// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. That is\n// rejected. The endangered version arrives via gossip (another replica\n// performed a merge write that advanced n1's self counter), which is\n// exactly the re-join window where the protection matters.\nfunc TestSameAuthorStaleContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1 := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil) // n1#1 {n1:1}\n\n\t// While n1 is partitioned, another replica advances n1's self counter\n\t// in a merge write and gossips the pure descendant n1#2 {n1:2} back.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(Snapshot{Versions: map[string][]Version{\n\t\t\"k\": {{ID: \"n1#2\", Value: raw(`\"b\"`), Clock: vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 2}, Author: \"n1\"}},\n\t}})\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\")\n\n\t// A stale client that only ever saw n1#1 now writes. The new clock\n\t// would be {n1:3}, silently dominating the unseen n1#2 -> rejected.\n\t_, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"c\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"})\n\tif rejectReason(t, err) != \"stale_context\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"want stale_context, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar rej *RejectError\n\terrors.As(err, &rej)\n\tif rej.StaleUnseen == nil || rej.StaleUnseen.ID != \"n1#2\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"rejection should name n1#2 as endangered, got %+v\", rej.StaleUnseen)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\") // store unchanged\n\n\t// Full context resolves cleanly.\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"c\"`), []string{\"n1#2\"}); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#3\")\n}","new_string":"// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version whose clock extends THIS node's self counter would give the new\n// clock a higher self counter and silently dominate it. a merge write with the\n// full context replaces both with one descendant.\nfunc TestOfflineWritesThenMerge(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1, n2 := NewStore(\"n1\"), NewStore(\"n2\")\n\n\tif _, err := n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"A\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"B\"`), nil); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\n\t// n2 learns n1#1, which is concurrent with n2#1 -> siblings.\n\tn2.MergeSnapshot(n1.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", \"n2#1\")\n\n\t// Cross-node stale context (client only saw n2#1) does NOT silently\n\t// overwrite n1#1: the new clock {n2:2} is concurrent with {n1:1},\n\t// so the unseen version survives as an extra sibling branch.\n\trep, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"fork\"`), []string{\"n2#1\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"concurrent fork should be accepted, got %v\", err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#1\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\n\t// Full context -> one descendant replaces both.\n\trep, err = n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"AB\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#2\"})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\tif rep.NewVersion.ID != \"n2#3\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"new id=%s\", rep.NewVersion.ID)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n\tif vclock.Compare(rep.NewVersion.Clock, vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 3}) != vclock.EqualRel {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"clock=%v\", rep.NewVersion.Clock)\n\t}\n\n\t// Resolution propagates: n1's n1#1 gets pruned on merge.\n\tr := n1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r.Pruned) != 1 || r.Pruned[0] != \"n1#1\" {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"merge pruned=%v want [n1#1]\", r.Pruned)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#3\")\n}\n\n// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version authored on THIS node would give the new clock a higher self\n// counter and thereby silently dominate the unseen version. That is\n// rejected. The endangered version arrives via gossip (another replica\n// performed a merge write that advanced n1's self counter), which is\n// exactly the re-join window where the protection matters.\nfunc TestSameAuthorStaleContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1 := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil) // n1#1 {n1:1}\n\n\t// While n1 is partitioned, another replica advances n1's self counter\n\t// in a merge write and gossips the pure descendant n1#2 {n1:2} back.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(Snapshot{Versions: map[string][]Version{\n\t\t\"k\": {{ID: \"n1#2\", Value: raw(`\"b\"`), Clock: vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 2}, Author: \"n1\"}},\n\t}})\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n1#2\")\n\n\t// A stale client that only ever saw n1#1 now writes. then the OLD snapshot {n1#1} arrives late. n1#1 is\n\t// already known to n2 and now dominated: it's a no-op duplicate.\n\tif _, err := n2.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"1+2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\", \"n2#1\"}); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatal(err)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\tr3 := n2.MergeSnapshot(s1)[\"k\"]\n\tif len(r3.Duplicate) != 1 || len(r3.Added) != 0 || len(r3.Pruned) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"late stale replay=%+v\", r3)\n\t}\n\texpectIDs(t, n2.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n\n\t// A genuinely OLD node receiving a descendant snapshot prunes the\n\t// ancestor locally.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(n2.Snapshot())\n\texpectIDs(t, n1.Read(\"k\"), \"n2#2\")\n}\n\n// Cross-node stale write forks; n3 does not see either.\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"2\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"3\"`), []string{\"n1#2\"}) // n1#3\n\n\t// n3 writes from the stale context [n1#1]. {"parentUuid":"05b99fed-0964-45d4-8b3a-d13b0af13bd8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_kaf91itdg1pm1hf4dmlf2b2c","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp24/b/internal/register/register_test.go","old_string":"// Same-author stale write: a write whose context omits a surviving\n// version whose clock extends THIS node's self counter would give the new\n// clock a higher self counter and silently dominate it. The dangerous\n// window is a node re-joining gossip: a merge write performed on another\n// replica advanced n1's counter inside a version whose clock also\n// carries components that keep the old sibling alive locally.\nfunc TestSameAuthorStaleContextRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\tn1 := NewStore(\"n1\")\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"a\"`), nil) // n1#1 {n1:1}\n\t// n1 branches offline too, so the incoming descendant below will not\n\t// transitively prune n1#1 on arrival (its n2 component dominates it\n\t// instead — it stays a sibling).\n\t_, _ = n1.Write(\"k\", raw(`\"local\"`), []string{\"n1#1\"}) // n1#2 {n1:2}\n\n\t// Another replica resolved against n1#1 jointly with its own branch,\n\t// producing n2#1 {n1:1,n2:1} — and then a merge write on that replica\n\t// advanced n1's counter to 3 with full coverage of n1#1/n2#1.\n\tn1.MergeSnapshot(Snapshot{Versions: map[string][]Version{\n\t\t\"k\": {\n\t\t\t{ID: \"n2#1\", Value: raw(`\"r\"`), Clock: vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 1, \"n2\": 1}, Author: \"n2\"},\n\t\t\t{ID: \"n1#3\", Value: raw(`\"b\"`), Clock: vclock.Clock{\"n1\": 3, \"n2\": 1}, Author: \"n1\"},\n\t\t},\n\t}})\n\t// n1#3 dominates n2#1; n1#2 {n1:2} is concurrent with n1#3 (the n2\n\t// component makes n1#2 <= n1#3 false on the n2 axis).
